findings.title: Breaking change details vanish undetected
findings.description: `auditNotes` compares JSON entries without their `breakingNotes` and collects only Markdown lines beginning `- `, excluding the indented lines that render those notes. If a breaking-change detail is omitted or changed in the saved outputs, every audit check can still pass even though readers receive incomplete release notes.

citations.citation:
const commits: [string, string][] = [
  [sha('a'), 'feat(cli): add check (#28)
'],
  [sha('b'), 'fix: escape more
'],
  [sha('c'), 'Merge pull request #28 from o/b
'],
  [sha('d'), 'Journl day 11 update
'],
  [sha('e'), 'feat!: drop old syntax

BREAKING CHANGE: the old syntax is gone
'],
];

evidence.explanation: Breaking-change footer values are preserved in group entries and rendered into both output formats, but the new audit omits the JSON field and skips the Markdown continuation lines. The test input already contains a breaking-change footer, making the omission reachable with the existing fixture.

findings.title: Audit requests can run shell commands
findings.description: The skill tells the agent to paste caller-provided range and output-directory values into single-quoted Bash assignments without shell-escaping them. A value containing a quote can end the assignment and execute a command before Git validates the range or the directory check runs.

citations.citation:
- **Range (required), in one of exactly two forms:** `<from>..<to>` (commits after `<from>` up
  to `<to>`) or a single `<rev>` (its whole history). Each endpoint is one revision git can
  resolve to a commit: a SHA, a branch, a tag, `HEAD~20`. Other range syntax (`A...B`, `HEAD^!`,
  `^A B`, several revisions) is not accepted: ask the human to restate it in one of the two
  forms (Qodo local review finding 9e7b46de).
- **Output directory (optional).** Default `evidence/audits/<from-short>-<to-short>/`, or
  `evidence/audits/root-<rev-short>/` for a single rev. On a hackathon day, the human may name
  `evidence/dayNN/audit-<label>/` instead.

Run each block from the repository root and check its result before the next one. **Every block
starts by setting its own values** (`RANGE`, `OUT`, `REPO_URL`), written out literally: the
agent's shell does not keep variables from one call to the next (Claude Code's Bash tool starts
each call fresh; Qodo local review finding 285ab321). Decide the three values in step 1 and
paste the same literal values at the top of every later block.

1. **Resolve the range and record the code version.**
   ```bash
   RANGE='<from>..<to>'                                  # or a single rev
   for end in $(printf '%s\n' "$RANGE" | sed 's/\.\./ /'); do git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$end^{commit}" || echo "UNRESOLVED $end"; done
   echo "commits: $(git rev-list --count "$RANGE")"

2. **Create the output directory** (refuse a non-empty one).
   ```bash
   OUT='evidence/audits/<from-short>-<to-short>'
   if [ -n "$(ls -A "$OUT" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then echo "NOT EMPTY: $OUT"; else mkdir -p "$OUT" && echo "created $OUT"; fi

5. **Run the audit** against the stated repository URL.
   ```bash
   OUT='evidence/audits/<from-short>-<to-short>'; REPO_URL='https://github.com/UBayouski/tracenotes'
   node .claude/skills/release-notes-audit/scripts/audit.ts "$OUT" "$REPO_URL" > "$OUT/audit.txt"; echo "audit exit $?"; cat "$OUT/audit.txt"

evidence.explanation: The instructions require literal values in each shell block, but place RANGE in Bash source before the rev-parse check and OUT in Bash source before the directory check. For example, substituting `HEAD'; printf 'INJECTED\n'; #` into the range assignment runs printf before rev-parse; the later Git failure cannot undo that execution. The optional output directory is likewise caller-selected and assigned before any check.

+   for end in $(printf '%s\n' "$RANGE" | sed 's/\.\./ /'); do git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$end^{commit}" || echo "UNRESOLVED $end"; done

findings.title: A token in the stated repo URL is printed
findings.description: `auditNotes` passes `input.repoUrl` to `checkRepoUrl`, whose `RangeError` includes the rejected value, and `run` prints that message unchanged to stderr. When the URL contains userinfo such as `https://user:token@github.com/o/r`, the token reaches stderr and, because SKILL.md step 5 tells the agent to report the error, can also reach the human conversation.

citations.citation: - Never print the origin remote itself: it can hold credentials. `render --origin` drops them.

The exit status is read with `$?` straight after the command, not through a pipe
   (finding facfcef8). Expected: five `PASS` lines and `audit: PASS`, exit 0. A range of only
   merge commits needs no special handling: there are no entries to link, and the URL is still
   checked as input. On exit 2, `audit.txt` is empty and the error is on the screen: report it.

export function auditNotes(input: AuditInput): AuditResult {
  checkRepoUrl(input.repoUrl);

evidence.explanation: `REPO_URL` allows only `[A-Za-z0-9.-]+` in the host, so a URL containing userinfo is rejected; `checkRepoUrl` includes the full input in its `RangeError`, and the audit entry point prints `error.message` unchanged. SKILL.md step 5 instructs the agent to report the error to the human, while the skill also warns that an origin remote can contain credentials.

findings.title: Wrong text after a subject passes the audit
findings.description: `mdWrongContent` compares only the start of an unescaped entry line through `- <scope><subject> (`, while `linkRe` and `anyCommitLink` check only commit links. Extra text between the subject and its commit link or after an otherwise correct entry, as well as a PR link with the wrong number or host, can therefore pass `markdown-links` despite changing the displayed text or source.

citations.citation: | `markdown-links` | Markdown entry line k is `group`'s entry k: under its section heading, with its scope and subject (escapes removed) and exactly one commit link, its own | a line has no link, two links, another commit's link, or the wrong heading, scope or subject |
release-notes-audit

| `json-links` | JSON entry k is `group`'s entry k: same commit, section, subject and scope, and its `commitUrl` is `<repo>/commit/<its sha>` | a link is wrong, an entry is not in the range, out of order, or under another section or subject |
| `markdown-links` | Markdown entry line k is `group`'s entry k: under its section heading, with its scope and subject (escapes removed) and exactly one commit link, its own | a line has no link, two links, another commit's link, or the wrong heading, scope or subject |

evidence.explanation: The renderer builds each line as `- ${scope}${escapeText(subject)} (${sourceText(source)})`, with `sourceText` supplying the commit link and, when known, a PR link. The audit compares only the prefix ending at ` (` and counts recognized commit links independently, so inserted or appended text does not affect either check; it does not check the PR link at all. This falls short of the skill table's claim that the check proves an entry shows its scope, subject, and own source link.

findings.title: Wrong Markdown footer counts go unnoticed
findings.description: `auditNotes` reads `notes.md` headings and entry lines but never parses its footer counts. If the rendered footer misstates shown, total, merge-ignored, config-ignored or malformed counts, the audit can still pass while the saved Markdown disagrees with the range and other outputs.

citations.citation: description: Audit the release notes tracenotes renders for one git range against the range itself - every commit accounted for exactly once, every entry linked to its own commit, all counts equal. Use after a change to parsing, grouping, rendering or the check command, before a release, or when asked to "audit the notes", "check the notes for <range>" or "prove nothing vanished". Needs a git range; saves the outputs and a PASS/FAIL report under evidence/.
release-notes-audit

## What each check proves

| Check | Proves | Fails when |
|---|---|---|
| `exactly-once` | every commit of the range appears once in `group` (a section or ignored) and nothing else does | a commit is missing, extra or listed twice, or a record was malformed |
| `counts` | `group`, `notes.json` and `check` count the range's size; `shown + ignored = total` | any count differs |
| `json-links` | JSON entry k is `group`'s entry k: same commit, section, subject and scope, and its `commitUrl` is `<repo>/commit/<its sha>` | a link is wrong, an entry is not in the range, out of order, or under another section or subject |
| `markdown-links` | Markdown entry line k is `group`'s entry k: under its section heading, with its scope and subject (escapes removed) and exactly one commit link, its own | a line has no link, two links, another commit's link, or the wrong heading, scope or subject |

evidence.explanation: `renderMarkdown` writes the user-facing count footer, but the audit’s count check compares the range, `group.json`, `notes.json` and `check.txt` without reading that footer. Its Markdown check examines headings, entry lines and links, so changing only a footer number affects none of the checks despite the stated expectation that the outputs’ counts agree.

findings.title: Moving branches change the audited range
findings.description: The skill resolves and counts `RANGE` in step 1, then resolves its names again for both saved git outputs in step 3. If a branch or tag moves between those steps, the audit can pass for a different commit set than the one initially counted and identified as the requested range.

citations.citation:
- **Range (required), in one of exactly two forms:** `<from>..<to>` (commits after `<from>` up
  to `<to>`) or a single `<rev>` (its whole history). Each endpoint is one revision git can
  resolve to a commit: a SHA, a branch, a tag, `HEAD~20`. Other range syntax (`A...B`, `HEAD^!`,
  `^A B`, several revisions) is not accepted: ask the human to restate it in one of the two
  forms (Qodo local review finding 9e7b46de).

1. **Resolve the range and record the code version.**
   ```bash
   RANGE='<from>..<to>'                                  # or a single rev
   for end in $(printf '%s\n' "$RANGE" | sed 's/\.\./ /'); do git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$end^{commit}" || echo "UNRESOLVED $end"; done
   echo "commits: $(git rev-list --count "$RANGE")"
   git rev-parse HEAD; git status --short -- src tests .claude
   ```
   Expected: no `UNRESOLVED` line and a count greater than 0. Stop otherwise. Note whether
   `src/` has uncommitted changes: the audit then covers the working tree, not `HEAD`. Choose
   `OUT` now: `evidence/audits/<from-short>-<to-short>` (short SHAs from `git rev-parse --short`)
   unless the human named another directory.

3. **Save the range and the stream.**
   ```bash
   RANGE='<from>..<to>'; OUT='evidence/audits/<from-short>-<to-short>'
   git rev-list "$RANGE" > "$OUT/rev-list.txt"
   git log --format='%H%x1f%an%x1f%aI%x1f%B%x1e' "$RANGE" > "$OUT/stream.bin"
   echo "rev-list lines: $(wc -l < "$OUT/rev-list.txt")"; ls -l "$OUT"
   ```
   Expected: the line count equals the count from step 1, and both files are in `$OUT`.

evidence.explanation: The skill permits branches and tags as endpoints, but its initial count and later evidence commands independently pass their names to git; the audit compares only the later saved outputs, not their identity against the earlier resolution.

findings.title: Misclassified notes pass the audit
findings.description: `auditNotes()` flattens the grouped and JSON sections before comparing SHAs, while its Markdown check ignores section headings. If rendering moves an entry into another section without changing the overall entry order, the audit passes despite the release notes assigning that commit to the wrong category.

evidence.explanation: Grouping assigns entries to named sections and rendering preserves those sections, but the audit compares flattened SHA arrays and filters Markdown down to entry lines.

findings.title: The real-range audit run is not saved with the PR
findings.description: The PR adds the release-notes-audit skill and its tests, but no saved audit output for a real repository range is in the diff. The only evidence under `evidence/day13/` is a test run and a `check` run, and neither is an audit of a range; the skill's required `audit.txt`, `notes.json`, `group.json` and the other evidence files are absent. The PR author's notes say the fresh-session run is deferred until after the merge, so this is a planned gap rather than an oversight, but the verification criterion is still unmet at the point this PR is reviewed. Until that run is saved, the skill has only been dry-run from the drafting session, and those dry-run results are not stored as evidence.

findings.title: Error line can carry bidi or line-separator text
findings.description: `run` formats the error with `JSON.stringify(message).slice(1, -1)`. That escapes C0 controls but leaves bidi overrides, zero-width characters, C1 controls and U+2028/U+2029 raw. The message can contain a rev-list.txt line (`rev-list.txt: "..." is not a full lowercase SHA`) or the `<dir>` path from a readFileSync error, so the promised single `error:` line can be visually spoofed or split.

citations.citation: if (!SHA_RE.test(line)) throw new RangeError(`rev-list.txt: ${JSON.stringify(line)} is not a full lowercase SHA`);
Diagnostics there also put raw file-derived text into one-line reports, so the line could be split or spoofed.

evidence.explanation: src/cli.ts defines `oneLine()` for exactly this: it applies JSON.stringify and then escapes what JSON leaves raw (bidi, C1, U+2028), for messages built from file content or paths. audit.ts uses only JSON.stringify. PR #24 had the same unescaped path or content problem in diagnostics.

location.code_snippet:
+    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
+    return { code: 2, stdout: '', stderr: `error: ${JSON.stringify(message).slice(1, -1)}\n` };

findings.title: Some malformed JSON throws TypeError, not RangeError
findings.description: `auditNotes` reads a section’s `title` and destructures entries before verifying that those values are non-null objects, so null members in parsed JSON throw `TypeError` rather than the documented `RangeError`. This affects null sections or entries in `group.json` and null entries in `notes.json`; because `run` catches every error and maps it to exit 2, callers cannot distinguish invalid input from a script bug.

citations.citation:
* @throws RangeError when an input cannot be read: a rev-list line that is not a full lowercase
 *         SHA, an empty range, JSON that does not parse or lacks a field, no `checked <n>:` line in
 *         the check output, or a repository URL `checkRepoUrl()` rejects. Nothing is guessed.
 */

evidence.explanation: `parseJson` accepts JSON nulls, and `field()` checks that `sections` is an array but does not validate its members. The subsequent direct `title` access and entry destructuring can therefore throw `TypeError` on a null member, despite the documented `RangeError` contract for input that cannot be read; `run` then catches that error along with all others.
